query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Inducing Cu segregation via a controlled pre-annealing treatment will promote the formation of Cu‐rich oxide films at grain boundaries during high-temperature sliding, which in turn reduces both overall wear and microscopic deformation compared to the baseline coating with a homogeneous element distribution.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate in its as-deposited baseline state with a near-homogeneous elemental distribution.
generation.intervention: Perform a controlled pre-annealing treatment at a temperature high enough to drive Cu segregation to grain boundaries relative to the untreated baseline coating.
generation.conditions: Operate under the intended high-temperature sliding regime (i.e., temperature high enough to facilitate oxide formation and grain boundary segregation, with controlled sliding speed and load as defined by the service conditions).
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced Cu enrichment at grain boundaries leading to in-situ formation of protective Cu‐rich oxide films during sliding.
generation.mechanism: Pre-annealing drives Cu segregation, which upon exposure to high-temperature sliding oxidizes preferentially to form a thin, protective oxide layer at grain boundaries. This layer mitigates metal-to-metal contact, reducing localized plastic deformation and wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under high-temperature sliding, the pre-annealed coating should exhibit a reduced wear rate and lower microscopic deformation compared to the baseline untreated coating.
generation.baseline: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating without any pre-annealing treatment, having a homogeneous distribution of elements.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies in the high-temperature sliding regime where oxidation kinetics and diffusion are active; different regime conditions (e.g., significantly lower temperatures) may not enable effective Cu segregation or oxide layer formation.
generation.uncertainty: While the qualitative improvement in wear resistance and deformation by enhanced Cu segregation is predicted, the precise magnitude of the effect is uncertain and likely depends on the extent of segregation and oxide film formation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set undergoes the controlled pre-annealing treatment to induce Cu segregation, and the control set remains in the as-deposited state. Subject both sets to identical high-temperature sliding tests while monitoring wear and microscopic deformation.
measurements: Wear rate quantification via mass loss or dimensional analysis
Microscopic assessment of deformation (e.g., scanning electron microscopy)
Grain boundary composition and oxide layer detection using techniques such as EDS or XPS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pre-annealed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in wear or microscopic deformation compared to the baseline, or if subsequent analysis does not show enhanced Cu segregation and oxide formation, the hypothesis is falsified.
